question: What is the primary cause of occupational lung diseases?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes without using a proper filter
options.B: Breathing in harmful workplace dusts and chemicals
options.C: Severe bacterial infections caught in the community
options.D: Inherited genetic defects of the respiratory tract

explanation: These conditions are directly caused by inhaling hazardous substances present in the work environment over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is early recognition of occupational lung diseases so critical for patients?

options.A: Treatment only works during the first week of coughing
options.B: The lung tissue scarring is usually permanent once it forms
options.C: Employers will immediately pay compensation before it spreads
options.D: Infections will spread to the brain within a few hours

explanation: Because the damage caused by dust accumulation leads to irreversible fibrosis, catching the condition early helps prevent further exposure and worsening illness. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which size of inhaled dust particles is most dangerous because it reaches the alveoli?

options.B: Large clumps visible to the naked human eye
options.C: Moisture droplets trapped in the nasal hair

explanation: Very small respirable dust particles bypass upper airway defenses and travel deep into the gas-exchanging regions of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h2)

question: What happens when alveolar macrophages try to swallow heavy loads of mineral dust?

options.A: They burst and release chemicals that cause scar tissue formation
options.B: They travel out of the lungs through the sweat glands
options.C: They turn into red blood cells to improve oxygen transport
options.D: They successfully dissolve the mineral dust into harmless sugar

explanation: When macrophages cannot digest toxic dust like silica, they break down and release inflammatory signals that trigger permanent lung fibrosis. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which group of occupational lung diseases is caused by inhaling mineral dusts like silica and asbestos?
explanation: Pneumoconiosis is the medical term for fibrotic lung diseases caused by the accumulation of mineral dusts in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: A baker who develops sudden wheezing and chest tightness after inhaling flour dust at work is most likely suffering from which condition?
explanation: Exposure to organic sensitizers like flour triggers an allergic airway response characterized by bronchospasm, which defines occupational asthma. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a major source of crystalline silica dust exposure for workers in many Nigerian local communities?

options.A: Operating commercial transport buses in traffic
options.B: Fishing in coastal rivers and marine lagoons
options.C: Artisanal gold mining and stone quarrying
options.D: Weaving traditional cotton fabrics by hand

explanation: Unregulated mining and quarrying activities frequently expose local Nigerian workers to high levels of dangerous silica dust. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why are informal sector workers in developing regions often at a higher risk for occupational lung disease?

options.A: Government laws completely ban safety masks in local factories
options.B: The tropical climate causes dust particles to become radioactive
options.C: They frequently lack proper personal protective equipment and health monitoring
options.D: Their lungs are naturally weaker than those of corporate office workers

explanation: The absence of safety gear, safety regulations, and routine medical checkups in informal industries greatly increases the risk of chronic lung injury. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is typically the earliest symptom experienced by someone developing an occupational lung disease?

options.A: A persistent cough and shortness of breath with exertion
options.B: Sudden paralysis of both lower extremities
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of taste and smell
options.D: Bright yellow coloration of the skin and eyes

explanation: Early lung damage usually manifests as a mild, dry cough and breathlessness that only appears when the person engages in physical work or exercise. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is taking a thorough work history so crucial when diagnosing respiratory problems?

options.A: Many lung diseases take years to develop and link directly to past job exposures
options.B: Work history determines the exact blood type of the individual
options.C: Doctors are legally required to record the patient's salary level
options.D: It helps prove whether the patient has a contagious viral infection

explanation: Because symptoms often appear long after the actual dust exposure occurred, a detailed job history is the key to identifying the root cause. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the most important first step in managing any patient diagnosed with an occupational lung disease?

options.A: Transferring the patient to a warm tropical climate
options.B: Removing the worker from further exposure to the harmful dust
options.C: Advising the patient to start smoking tobacco to coat the lungs

explanation: Stopping ongoing exposure to the hazardous agent is essential to prevent further lung destruction and worsening fibrosis. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse is teaching breathing techniques to a patient with severe lung fibrosis. Which method should the nurse demonstrate to help ease shortness of breath?

options.A: Holding the breath for two minutes after each deep sigh
options.B: Breathing exclusively through the mouth while running fast
options.C: Rapid shallow panting to increase carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Pursed-lip breathing to help keep airways open longer

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates gentle backpressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing prematurely and easing shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the term for right-sided heart failure caused by long-term lung disease?
explanation: Cor pulmonale refers to enlargement and failure of the right ventricle resulting from high blood pressure in the pulmonary blood vessels due to lung disease. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why do patients with advanced occupational lung diseases have an increased risk of heart failure?

options.A: Respiratory failure lowers the body temperature until the heart stops beating
options.B: The inhaled mineral dust travels directly into the heart muscle and clogs valves
options.C: Scarred lung tissue restricts blood flow, forcing the right heart to pump much harder
options.D: Lung damage causes the patient to drink excessive amounts of salty water

explanation: Destruction of the pulmonary capillary bed increases vascular resistance, putting immense strain on the right side of the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is considered the single most effective approach to managing occupational lung diseases?

options.B: Performing routine lung transplant surgery on all workers
options.C: Administering oxygen therapy during night shifts only
options.D: Primary prevention and stopping exposure to dust

explanation: Because lung scarring cannot be reversed, stopping the inhalation of harmful dusts before disease starts is the only foolproof solution. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of routine spirometry testing in an industrial occupational health clinic?

options.A: To test the employee's hearing capacity against machine noise
options.B: To check if the worker has contracted a stomach ulcer
options.C: To measure the exact body weight and fat percentage of workers
options.D: To detect early drops in lung function before symptoms appear

explanation: Regular spirometry allows nurses and occupational health officers to spot early breathing impairments so corrective safety steps can be taken immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)
